previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of end-stage renal disease, polycystic kidney disease, and refractory atrial fibrillation was admitted due to atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response that prevented her from receiving scheduled dialysis. She reported two weeks of palpitations, fatigue, nausea, and one day of chills. Her potassium was elevated at 5.9 mEq/L on arrival, prompting treatment with kayexalate and urgent hemodialysis. Blood cultures showed no growth, and her chest X-ray revealed mild interstitial pulmonary edema. The cardiology team advanced her planned ablation procedure. Metoprolol dosing was adjusted to include 25 mg on dialysis days. She completed dialysis, stabilized hemodynamically, and was discharged home with instructions to continue medications, attend dialysis, monitor weight, and prepare for ablation.
